questions.question: 'Spin only' magnetic moment is same for which of the following ions? A. Ti³⁺, B. Cr²⁺, C. Mn²⁺, D. Fe²⁺, E. Sc³⁺
questions.explanation: μ = √(n(n+2)) BM. Ti³⁺(3d¹)=n1, Cr²⁺(3d⁴)=n4, Mn²⁺(3d⁵)=n5, Fe²⁺(3d⁶)=n4, Sc³⁺(3d⁰)=n0. Cr²⁺ and Fe²⁺ both have n=4, so same magnetic moment.

questions.question: The most stable carbocation among the following is: (options show different carbocations with varying structures)

options.A: Tertiary carbocation with 3 methyl groups (neopentyl type)

questions.explanation: The most stable carbocation is the tropylium cation (aromatic 6π electrons) with extended resonance giving highest stability (αH=7).

questions.question: Statement-I: The boiling point of hydrides of Group-16 elements follow the order H₂O > H₂Te > H₂Se > H₂S. Statement-II: On the basis of molecular mass, H₂O is expected to have lower boiling point than the other members of the group but due to the presence of extensive H-bonding in H₂O, it has higher boiling point.

options.A: Both statement-I and Statement-II are true
options.B: Both statement-I and Statement-II are false
options.C: Statement-I is the true but Statement-II is false
options.D: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true

questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. H₂O has highest bp due to extensive H-bonding despite lowest molecular mass. Order: H₂O > H₂Te > H₂Se > H₂S.

questions.question: Match List I with List II (Compound and Shape/geometry): A. NI₃, B. BrF₅, C. XeF₄, D. SF₆ with I. Trigonal Pyramidal, II. Square Planar, III. Octahedral, IV. Square Pyramidal
questions.explanation: NI₃ (sp³+1LP)=Trigonal Pyramidal (I), BrF₅ (sp³d²+1LP)=Square Pyramidal (IV), XeF₄ (sp³d²+2LP)=Square Planar (II), SF₆ (sp³d²)=Octahedral (III).

questions.question: The highest number of helium atoms is in:
questions.explanation: 4 mol He = 4 × 6.022×10²³ atoms. 4u He = 1 atom. 4g He = NA atoms. 0.1mol He = 0.1NA atoms. Largest is 4 mol = 4NA atoms.

questions.question: Identify the correct reagents that would bring about the following transformation: Benzyl allyl → Benzyl propan-1-al (CH₂-CH₂-CHO)
questions.explanation: Hydroboration-oxidation (anti-Markovnikov) gives primary alcohol, then PCC oxidizes primary alcohol to aldehyde.

questions.question: Match List I (Process) with List II (Conditions): A. Isothermal process, B. Isochoric process, C. Isobaric process, D. Adiabatic process with I. No heat exchange, II. Carried out at constant temperature, III. Carried out at constant volume, IV. Carried out at constant pressure
questions.explanation: Isothermal=constant temperature (II), Isochoric=constant volume (III), Isobaric=constant pressure (IV), Adiabatic=no heat exchange (I).

questions.question: Which one one of the following alcohols reacts instantaneously with Lucas reagent?
questions.explanation: Lucas reagent reactivity: 3° > 2° > 1°. (CH₃)₃C-OH is tertiary alcohol and reacts instantaneously with ZnCl₂/HCl.

questions.question: In which of the following equilibria, Kp and Kc are NOT equal?
questions.explanation: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δng. When Δng≠0, Kp≠Kc. Only PCl₅ dissociation has Δng=1 (2-1=1). Others have Δng=0.

questions.question: Match List I (Quantum Number) with List II (Information provided): A. mℓ, B. ms, C. ℓ, D. n with I. shape of orbital, II. size of orbital, III. orientation of orbital, IV. orientation of spin of electron
questions.explanation: mℓ=orientation of orbital (III), ms=orientation of spin (IV), ℓ=shape of orbital (I), n=size of orbital (II).

questions.question: Statement I: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction. Statement II: Aniline cannot be prepared through Gabriel synthesis.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true

questions.explanation: Both true. Aniline forms complex with AlCl₃ (Lewis acid), so F-C reaction fails. Gabriel synthesis uses aryl halides which are poor SN2 substrates.

questions.question: Intramolecular hydrogen bonding is present in:
questions.explanation: o-nitrophenol has intramolecular H-bonding between -OH and -NO₂ groups in ortho position (within the same molecule).

questions.question: On heating, some solid substances change from solid to vapour state without passing through liquid state. The technique used for the purification of such solid substances based on the above principle is known as:
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the process of solid converting directly to vapour without passing through liquid state, used for purification of substances like camphor, iodine.

questions.question: In which of the following processes entropy increases? A. A liquid evaporates to vapour, B. Temperature of a crystalline solid lowered from 130K to 0K, C. 2NaHCO₃(s) → Na₂CO₃(s) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(g), D. Cl₂(g) → 2Cl(g)
questions.explanation: Entropy increases when: A (liquid to vapour - more disorder), C (solid → gas products, Δng=+2), D (1 molecule → 2 atoms, more disorder). B decreases entropy (lower temperature, more order).

questions.question: Among Group 16 elements, which one does NOT show –2 oxidation state?
questions.explanation: Polonium (Po) does not show -2 oxidation state due to its metallic nature. O, S, Se, Te all show -2 state.

questions.question: Match List-I (Conversion) with List-II (Number of Faraday required): A. 1 mol H₂O to O₂, B. 1 mol MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁺, C. 1.5 mole of Ca from molten CaCl₂, D. 1 mol of FeO to Fe₂O₃
questions.explanation: H₂O→O₂: 2F per mol H₂O (II), MnO₄⁻→Mn²⁺: 5F (IV), 1.5mol Ca: 1.5×2=3F (I), FeO→Fe₂O₃: Fe²⁺→Fe³⁺, 1F (III).

questions.question: Arrange the following elements in increasing order of electronegativity: N, O, F, C, Si
questions.explanation: Electronegativity (Pauling scale): Si(1.8) < C(2.5) < N(3.0) < O(3.5) < F(4.0).

questions.question: A compound with a molecular formula of C₆H₁₄ has two tertiary carbons. Its IUPAC name is:
questions.explanation: 2,3-dimethylbutane: CH₃-CH(CH₃)-CH(CH₃)-CH₃ has two tertiary carbons (C2 and C3, each bonded to 3 carbons).

questions.question: Fehling's solution 'A' is

options.C: alkaline solution of sodium potassium tartrate (Rochelle's salt)

questions.explanation: Fehling solution A = aqueous copper sulphate (CuSO₄). Fehling B = alkaline sodium potassium tartrate (Rochelle's salt).

questions.question: Activation energy of any chemical reaction can be calculated if one knows the value of

options.C: orientation of reactant molecules during collision
options.D: rate constant at two different temperatures

questions.explanation: Using Arrhenius equation: log(k₂/k₁) = (Ea/2.303R)(1/T₁ - 1/T₂). Need rate constants at two temperatures to calculate Ea.

questions.question: Which plot of ln k vs 1/T is consistent with Arrhenius equation?

options.D: Straight line with negative slope going through positive y-intercept

questions.explanation: ln k = lnA - Ea/RT = lnA - (Ea/R)(1/T). This is y=mx+c where slope = -Ea/R (NEGATIVE). Graph of lnk vs 1/T gives straight line with negative slope.

questions.question: Match List I (Reaction) with List II (Reagents/Condition): A. Benzene→2 benzaldehyde, B. Benzene→benzophenone, C. Cyclohexanol→cyclohexanone, D. Xylene→potassium benzoate
questions.explanation: Benzene→2benzaldehyde (reductive ozonolysis=O₃/Zn-H₂O) (IV), Benzene→benzophenone (Friedel-Craft acylation=COCl/AlCl₃) (I), Cyclohexanol→ketone (CrO₃ mild oxidation) (II), Xylene→COOK (KMnO₄/KOH,Δ) (III).

questions.question: The compound that will undergo SN1 reaction with the fastest rate is:
questions.explanation: SN1 rate ∝ carbocation stability. Benzyl cation with p-methyl group has extended resonance (resonance + 4αH stabilization), making it most stable and fastest SN1.

questions.question: Which reaction is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl is a double displacement (precipitation) reaction with no change in oxidation states.

questions.question: Statement I: The boiling point of three isomeric pentanes follows the order n-pentane > isopentane > neopentane. Statement II: When branching increases, the molecule attains a shape of sphere resulting in smaller surface area, so intermolecular forces are weak, thereby lowering the boiling point.

options.A: Both statement I and Statement II are correct
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.explanation: Both correct. n-pentane (309K) > isopentane (301K) > neopentane (283K). Increased branching → spherical shape → less surface area → weaker van der Waals → lower bp.

questions.question: Statement I: Both [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ and [CoF₆]³⁻ complexes are octahedral but differ in their magnetic behaviour. Statement II: [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is diamagnetic whereas [CoF₆]³⁻ is paramagnetic.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.explanation: Both correct. Co³⁺ = 3d⁶. NH₃ is SFL → d²sp³, paired electrons → diamagnetic (μ=0). F⁻ is WFL → sp³d², unpaired → paramagnetic (μ=4.9 BM).

questions.question: Match List I (Molecule) with List II (Number and types of bonds between two carbon atoms): A. ethane, B. ethene, C. carbon molecule C₂, D. ethyne
questions.explanation: Ethane (C-C)=1σ bond (III), Ethene (C=C)=1σ+1π bonds (IV), C₂ molecule=2π bonds per MOT (II), Ethyne (C≡C)=1σ+2π bonds (I).

questions.question: The Henry's law constant (KH) values of three gases A, B, C in water are 145, 2×10⁻⁵ and 35 kbar, respectively. The solubility of these gases in water follow the order:
questions.explanation: Solubility ∝ 1/KH. Lower KH = higher solubility. B(2×10⁻⁵) < C(35) < A(145). So solubility order: B > C > A.

questions.question: The energy of an electron in the ground state (n=1) for He⁺ ion is -xJ, then that for an electron in n=2 state for Be³⁺ ion in J is:
questions.explanation: E = -13.6 × Z²/n² eV. He⁺: Z=2, n=1: E=-x. Be³⁺: Z=4, n=2: E ∝ Z²/n² = 4²/2² = 4. E(He⁺) ∝ 2²/1² = 4. Ratio = 1. So E(Be³⁺, n=2) = -x.

questions.question: The E° value for the Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺ couple is more positive than that of Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺ or Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ due to change of
questions.explanation: Mn³⁺(3d⁴) → Mn²⁺(3d⁵). The gain of extra stability of half-filled d⁵ configuration makes Mn³⁺ a stronger oxidizing agent (more positive E°).

questions.question: The reagents with which glucose does NOT react to give the corresponding tests/products are: A. Tollens' reagent, B. Schiff's reagent, C. HCN, D. NH₂OH, E. NaHSO₃
questions.explanation: Glucose does NOT react with Schiff's reagent (B) and NaHSO₃ (E) as it exists predominantly in cyclic form with no free aldehyde group easily accessible.

questions.question: Match List I (Complex) with List II (Type of isomerism): A. [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂, B. [Co(NH₃)₅(SO₄)]Br, C. [Co(NH₃)₆][Cr(CN)₆], D. [Co(H₂O)₆]Cl₃ with I. Solvate isomerism, II. Linkage isomerism, III. Ionization isomerism, IV. Coordination isomerism
questions.explanation: [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂: NO₂ can be NO₂ or ONO (Linkage II), [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br: ionization isomer with [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄ (Ionization III), [Co(NH₃)₆][Cr(CN)₆]: coordination isomerism (IV), [Co(H₂O)₆]Cl₃: solvate isomerism (I).

questions.question: Arrange the following elements in increasing order of first ionization enthalpy: Li, Be, B, C, N
questions.explanation: IE₁ order: Li < B < Be < C < N. Be has higher IE than B (Be=2s² full, B=2s²2p¹ easier to remove 2p). N higher than C (half-filled 2p³ extra stability).

questions.question: 1 gram of sodium hydroxide was treated with 25 mL of 0.75 M HCl solution, the mass of sodium hydroxide left unreacted is equal to
questions.explanation: Moles NaOH = 1/40 = 0.025 mol. Moles HCl = 0.75×25/1000 = 0.01875 mol. NaOH is excess. Unreacted NaOH = 0.025-0.01875 = 0.00625 mol = 0.00625×40 g = 0.25g = 250 mg.

questions.question: For the reaction 2A ⇌ B + C, Kc = 4×10⁻³. At a given time, the composition is [A]=[B]=[C]=2×10⁻³ M. Then which of the following is correct?

options.B: Reaction has a tendency to go in forward direction
options.C: Reaction has a tendency to go in backward direction
options.D: Reaction has gone to completion in forward direction

questions.explanation: Qc = [B][C]/[A]² = (2×10⁻³)(2×10⁻³)/(2×10⁻³)² = 1. Since Qc(1) > Kc(4×10⁻³), reaction tends to go backward.

questions.question: Given below are certain cations. Using inorganic qualitative analysis, arrange them in increasing group number from 0 to VI: A. Al³⁺, B. Cu²⁺, C. Ba²⁺, D. Co²⁺, E. Mg²⁺
questions.explanation: Group numbers: Cu²⁺=II, Al³⁺=III, Co²⁺=IV, Ba²⁺=V, Mg²⁺=VI. Increasing order: B(Cu²⁺), A(Al³⁺), D(Co²⁺), C(Ba²⁺), E(Mg²⁺).

questions.question: The products A and B obtained in the following reactions are: 3ROH + PCl₃ → 3RCl + A; ROH + PCl₅ → RCl + HCl + B
questions.explanation: 3ROH + PCl₃ → 3RCl + H₃PO₃ (A). ROH + PCl₅ → RCl + HCl + POCl₃ (B).

questions.question: Mass in grams of copper deposited by passing 9.6487 A current through a voltmeter containing copper sulphate solution for 100 seconds is: (Molar mass of Cu: 63 g mol⁻¹, 1F = 96487 C)

The plot of osmotic pressure (Π) vs concentration (mol L⁻¹) for a solution gives a straight line with slope 25.73 L bar mol⁻¹. The temperature at which the osmotic pressure measurement is done is: (R = 0.083 L bar mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
Identify the major product C formed in the following reaction sequence: CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-I + NaCN → A + OH⁻/Partial hydrolysis → B + NaOH/Br₂ → C (Major)
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂CH₂I + NaCN → CH₃CH₂CH₂CN (A). Partial hydrolysis → CH₃CH₂CH₂CONH₂ (B). Hofmann bromamide → CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂ (propylamine, C).

questions.question: Identify the correct answer.

options.A: Three resonance structures can be drawn for ozone
options.C: Dipole moment of NF₃ is greater than that of NH₃
options.D: Three canonical forms can be drawn for CO₃²⁻ ion

questions.explanation: CO₃²⁻ has three equivalent canonical/resonance structures. Ozone has 2 resonance structures. BF₃ is symmetrical (zero dipole). NH₃ > NF₃ in dipole moment.

questions.question: Statement I: [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is a homoleptic complex whereas [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ is a heteroleptic complex. Statement II: Complex [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ has only one kind of ligands but [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ has more than one kind of ligands.

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.explanation: Both correct. Homoleptic=only one type of ligand (NH₃ in [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺). Heteroleptic=more than one type (NH₃ and Cl⁻ in [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺).

questions.question: For the given reaction: Ph-C(=CH-Ph)-H + KMnO₄/H⁺ → P (major product). P is:
questions.explanation: KMnO₄/H⁺ (acidic) oxidizes alkene. Ph-CH=CH-Ph → 2 Ph-COOH (benzoic acid). Each carbon of alkene becomes carboxylate.

questions.question: The pair of lanthanoid ions which are diamagnetic is
questions.explanation: Ce⁴⁺ = [Xe]4f⁰ (no unpaired e⁻ = diamagnetic). Yb²⁺ = [Xe]4f¹⁴ (completely filled, no unpaired e⁻ = diamagnetic).

questions.question: Consider the reaction 2NO(g) ⇌ N₂(g) + O₂(g) at equilibrium with [N₂]=3×10⁻³M, [O₂]=4.2×10⁻³M, [NO]=2.8×10⁻³M. If 0.1 mol L⁻¹ of NO₂ is taken in a closed vessel, what will be degree of dissociation (α) of NO₂ at equilibrium?
A compound X contains 32% of A, 20% of B and remaining percentage of C. Then, the empirical formula of X is: (Given atomic masses of A=64, B=40, C=32u)
questions.explanation: A: 32/64 = 0.5 (ratio 1), B: 20/40 = 0.5 (ratio 1), C: 48/32 = 1.5 (ratio 3). Empirical formula = ABC₃.

questions.question: The work done during reversible isothermal expansion of one mole of hydrogen gas at 25°C from pressure of 20 atmosphere to 10 atmosphere is: (R = 2.0 cal K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
During the preparation of Mohr's salt solution (Ferrous ammonium sulphate), which of the following acid is added to prevent hydrolysis of Fe²⁺ ion?
questions.explanation: Dilute H₂SO₄ is added to prevent hydrolysis of Fe²⁺ ions. Concentrated H₂SO₄ would oxidize Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺. HCl and HNO₃ are not used.

questions.question: The rate of a reaction quadruples when temperature changes from 27°C to 57°C. Calculate the energy of activation. (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, log 4 = 0.6021)
Major products A and B formed in the following reaction sequence: 1-methylcyclohexanol + PBr₃ → A (major) + alc.KOH/heat → B (major)
questions.explanation: 1-methylcyclohexanol + PBr₃ → 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane (A, retention of configuration). Alc. KOH/heat = E2 elimination → 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene (B, Zaitsev product).
